target_customer: Makers and operators of small expendable UAVs and drones, mainly defense primes and integrators buying under US drone procurement programs
problem: Satellite positioning is a single point of failure for drones, and jamming or spoofing denies GPS in contested areas. Small drones need a cheap drop-in navigation module that works without satellites.
business_model: Hardware module sales (drop-in navigation unit) with contracted supply orders
product_category: GPS-denied visual or inertial navigation module for UAVs

founders.name: Gabriel Poraj
prior_employers: Torus (senior software developer, per YC page)
education: Cambridge, studying Aerospace/Information Engineering (per YC page)
previous_startups: Content agency for faceless creators (per YC page, outcome not stated)

founders.name: Charlie Jessett
founders.background_notes: YC page gives no employer history.

competitors.name: ANELLO Photonics
competitors.what: Aerial inertial navigation unit with PX4 and ArduPilot drivers and spoofing detection
competitors.traction_then: Evaluation kits shipping, production slated for Q2 2026

competitors.name: UNIBIRD N200M
competitors.what: Visual inertial navigation module connecting to PX4 or APM over MAVLink, priced at $399

competitors.name: Vydar
competitors.what: Computer vision edge AI GPS-free navigation module, 50x50 mm

technical_complexity.rationale: Reliable satellite-free positioning on small drones needs sensor fusion, vision or inertial algorithms and embedded integration with open flight stacks; the company claims demonstrated autonomous flight and GPS handoff, which is not independently verified.

defensibility.rationale: Several funded and launched modules already target PX4 and ArduPilot, and a two-person team has no data or regulatory moat yet. Contracted defense supply could add switching costs later.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Too early to know; the company is at the start of its batch.

market_need_then: Jamming and spoofing of GPS in current conflicts and a US Drone Dominance procurement program create demand for GPS-free navigation. The company says it has over $80k in contracted supply revenue, which is company-reported only.

branding.domain_note: Uses streamlinesystems.ltd rather than a .com; several unrelated companies use the name Streamline Systems.

identity.logo: Simple company logo on a landing page

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community about the brand found, and the generic name shares search space with unrelated firms.

outcome_analysis: The company is active at the start of its Fall 2026 batch with no exit and no public funding. Its prospects rest on the GPS-denied drone navigation tailwind and early contracted supply, set against several funded modules aimed at the same open flight controllers.
notes: No funding found beyond YC backing. A directory listing (nordic9) mentions one unnamed investor with no amount; unverified. The $80k contract figure is from the YC description only. No outcome news found (searched acquisition, shutdown, layoffs terms).
